subject: Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, released 2026-09-22
central_claim: Anthropic's 2026-09-22 Claude Opus 5.5 release is a publishable AI engineering topic because official Anthropic primary sources support a bounded E2/R1 claim: Opus 5.5 is positioned for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work, and its API contract changes always-on adaptive thinking, effort-based control, tool_choice behavior, computer-use toolset requirements, context/output limits and pricing. The article does not claim independent benchmark superiority over OpenAI, Google or previous Claude models.

selection.reason: Claude Opus 5.5 is a recent frontier-lab model release with concrete API migration details that affect long-running coding agents and knowledge-work products. It is not Korea-specific, but Korean software teams using Claude API, Bedrock, Google Cloud or agent coding products would need to re-check thinking, effort, tool_choice, computer-use toolsets and cost traces before migration.

claims.claim: Claude Opus 5.5 changes more than a model choice: for long-running coding and knowledge-work agents, Anthropic's official documents require teams to account for always-on adaptive thinking, effort-based control, tool_choice restrictions, computer-use toolset migration, 1M context, 128K output and revised token/cache pricing.

claim_source_ledger.claim: Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 5.5 on 2026-09-22 as the first model in its Claude 5.5 family.
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened the official Anthropic launch page and checked the title, publication date and introductory release statement.
limitations: Anthropic authors the launch page for its own model.
The page confirms release and vendor claims but does not independently verify model quality.
conflict_of_interest: Anthropic develops and sells access to Claude Opus 5.5.

claim_source_ledger.claim: Claude Platform release notes list `claude-opus-5-5` as a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work, with 1M token context, 128K max output tokens and always-on adaptive thinking.
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened the official Claude Platform release notes and read the September 22, 2026 Opus 5.5 entry.
limitations: No API call was run to verify account-level availability or token limits.
The claim is bounded to documented platform behavior.
conflict_of_interest: Anthropic controls the Claude Platform documentation.

claim_source_ledger.claim: For Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic documents that `thinking` cannot be disabled or explicitly enabled; developers should omit the `thinking` field and control thinking depth with the `effort` parameter.
claim_source_ledger.version: Claude Platform release notes, 2026-09-22 API migration notes
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the release-note bullet describing 400 errors for disabled or enabled thinking fields and the effort-parameter guidance.
limitations: The behavior was not reproduced with live API requests.
The article does not infer quality or latency effects beyond the documented contract.
conflict_of_interest: Anthropic documents the behavior of its own API.

claim_source_ledger.claim: Claude Opus 5.5 rejects `tool_choice` types `any` and `tool`, and computer use on the Claude API and Google Cloud requires `computer_toolset_20260801`; on Amazon Bedrock, `computer_20251124` remains supported.
claim_source_ledger.version: Claude Platform release notes, 2026-09-22 tool migration notes
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the official release-note bullets for tool_choice and computer-use toolset behavior.
limitations: No platform-specific request was executed on Claude API, Bedrock or Google Cloud.
The article treats this as migration guidance rather than a measured reliability improvement.
conflict_of_interest: Anthropic publishes the migration guidance for its model.

claim_source_ledger.claim: The Claude models overview describes Opus 5.5 as a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work and lists its API alias, cloud platform IDs, default effort, context window, max output, knowledge cutoff and retirement commitment.
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened the official model overview and read the current model comparison table.
limitations: Model overview is documentation, not an independent benchmark.
The article does not rely on the overview for performance superiority claims.

claim_source_ledger.claim: Claude Platform pricing lists Opus 5.5 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, with prompt cache writes and hits priced separately; it also notes that Claude 4.7 and later models use a newer tokenizer that can produce about 30% more tokens for the same text depending on workload.
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the pricing table and additional tokenizer note on the official pricing page.
limitations: Actual customer bills depend on tokenization, cache hit rates, effort, output length, platform and negotiated discounts.
No trace-based cost measurement was performed.
conflict_of_interest: Anthropic sells access to Claude models and publishes the pricing page.

claim_source_ledger.claim: Anthropic reports Opus 5.5 benchmark and early-tester results, but the article treats these as vendor-authored performance signals rather than independent evidence of general superiority.
claim_source_ledger.version: Claude Opus 5.5 launch page, benchmark and tester sections
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the benchmark table, footnotes and early-tester examples and restricted their use to context.
limitations: Benchmark and customer examples are not editor-run or independently reproduced in this turn.
Some reported comparisons depend on effort, safeguards, platform and evaluator-specific harnesses.
conflict_of_interest: Anthropic markets Claude Opus 5.5 and selected the presentation of benchmark and tester evidence.

benchmark_and_reproducibility.benchmark_notes: The article mentions Anthropic's benchmark surfaces only as context for what Anthropic claims. It does not make an editorial claim that Opus 5.5 is generally superior to GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5 or other models.
benchmark_and_reproducibility.reproducibility_notes: Official launch, release-note, model-overview and pricing documents are public and inspectable. The model weights, training data, evaluation harnesses, production safeguards and live API behavior were not reproduced. No Claude API account, Bedrock deployment or Google Cloud endpoint was used.

source_conflicts: Anthropic develops and sells Claude Opus 5.5 and authors the launch page, release notes, model overview and pricing documentation.
Other candidates reviewed included official source paths from OpenAI, Google, Mistral, vLLM, DeepSeek and Qwen.
access_conditions: No vendor briefing, embargo, paid account, credits, hardware or private documentation were used.
Only public official documents, release notes, model docs, pricing pages, GitHub release pages and search-discovered primary paths were used.

signals.note: Reviewed Mistral changelog and release-note surfaces. The visible current signal was mainly Vibe experience consolidation and earlier OCR/model updates; no fresher model/API/runtime topic beat Opus 5.5 on importance and decision utility.

Opened vLLM releases. v0.29.0 and v0.30.0 are strong implementation-backed runtime signals with Model Runner V2 and model support changes, but the public release was older in the window and more infrastructure-specific than the same-week frontier model API migration.

Search result snippets and general web results were used only to discover official primary-source URLs. Article facts and candidate scoring rely on opened official launch pages, platform docs, release notes, pricing pages and GitHub release pages.
